description: Verify the Source IP Address field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals the configured DIface-0 IPv4 — identifies the resolver's IP back to peers (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
The sender_ip field of an ARP Request is what receiving peers use to populate their own caches with '<sender_ip, sender_mac>'. DUT must put its outgoing-interface IPv4 there, not a placeholder or wrong-iface address. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the sender_ip.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back; cache miss forces an ARP Request.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode      == 1
      - sender_mac  == DUT iface MAC
      - sender_ip   == DIface-0 IPv4 (DUT outgoing iface)   ← key check
      - target_ip   == HOST-1-IP

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's sender_ip matches the DUT's configured DIface-0 IPv4.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_sender_ip — ARP Request seen but sender_ip differed from the iface address (e.g. 0.0.0.0 placeholder, multi-homed routing slipped, or stale binding)
• Fail_timeout — No DUT ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Pass: ARP Request sender_ip matched DIface-0 IPv4 — normal
verdicts.Fail_sender_ip: ARP Request emitted but sender_ip did not match DIface-0 IPv4
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
